QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_3

question.text: A bond portfolio worth Rs. 10 crore has a PV01 of Rs. 8,000. The cheapest-to-deliver bond futures contract has a PV01 of Rs. 80. How many futures contracts are needed to hedge the portfolio?

explanation.text: The Logic: PV01 (the price value of a 1 basis-point change) is the practical workbook measure on p. 64. A PV01-matched hedge requires Portfolio PV01 / Futures PV01 = 8,000 / 80 = 100 contracts. This is consistent with the duration-based hedge-ratio formula on pp. 164-165, since matching PV01s matches the rupee impact of a 1 bp move. The Trap: 1,000 incorrectly divides portfolio value by PV01. 125 mis-adjusts for lot size. 80 mistakenly uses the futures PV01 itself. Note: The workbook uses PV01 (pp. 63-64) and the duration-based hedge ratio (pp. 164-165); both yield the same hedge when applied consistently.
